desc: Newline-only tokens, including repeated line breaks.
Standalone ordinary-space tokens.
Standalone tabs or other horizontal whitespace.
Document boundaries and dedicated control or special tokens.
Replacement characters and visibly corrupted text fragments.
Sentence-ending periods and period punctuation clusters.
Comma punctuation, including comma-led clusters.
Colons and semicolons, including adjacent punctuation clusters.
Question marks and exclamation marks, including closing clusters.
Quotation marks, apostrophes, and quote-attached punctuation.
Opening parentheses, optionally with preceding whitespace.
Closing parentheses, optionally with following punctuation.
Opening square brackets, optionally with preceding whitespace.
Closing square brackets, optionally with following punctuation.
Opening braces, optionally with preceding whitespace.
Closing braces, optionally with following punctuation.
Hyphens, dashes, and their whitespace-prefixed forms.
Slash and backslash punctuation outside other clear roles.
Ellipses and non-sentence dot sequences.
Markdown emphasis, heading, fence, and inline-code markers.
Assignment, equality, and compound-assignment operators.
Arithmetic operators such as plus, minus, multiply, and modulo.
Comparison, logical, and arrow-like operators.
Code-context separators and punctuation not covered by bracket classes.
Currency symbols, percent signs, and numeric grouping punctuation.
Mathematical notation symbols outside ordinary arithmetic operators.
Single decimal digits, with or without a leading space.
Complete multi-digit numerals, years, and numeric constants.
Signs, decimal pieces, exponents, and other numeral fragments.
Spelled-out numbers, number names, and ordinal words.
Measurement units and conventional unit abbreviations.
Code-context booleans, nulls, and literal-value fragments.
Programming language keywords and declaration or control words.
Common programming builtins, library names, and callable primitives.
Code variables, functions, properties, and identifier fragments.
HTML, XML, and markup tag or attribute names.
Word-initial articles, demonstratives, quantifiers, and possessive determiners.
Word-initial personal, relative, and interrogative pronouns.
Word-initial prepositions and common prepositional particles.
Word-initial coordinating and subordinating conjunctions.
Word-initial auxiliary verbs, modals, and forms of be or have.
Word-initial negators, contractions, and short discourse particles.
Word-initial adverbs, intensifiers, and verb particles.
Word-initial lexical verbs and verb forms.
Word-initial common nouns and nominal forms.
Word-initial adjectives and participles used attributively.
Word-initial personal, place, organization, and product names.
Initialisms, all-capital abbreviations, and acronym fragments.
Capitalized common words beginning sentences or headings.
Unspaced complete grammatical words, including contractions.
Unspaced complete ordinary words not clearly names or code.
Unspaced lowercase pieces beginning words, judged from context.
Capitalized word fragments that continue names or words.
Word-final or word-internal pieces spelling the suffix -ing.
Pieces spelling common past-tense or participial endings.
Pieces spelling plural, possessive, or third-person endings.
Pieces spelling common derivational endings such as -tion or -ity.
Common word-initial prefixes attached to continuing words.
Lowercase alphabetic pieces continuing a word, excluding clear suffixes.
Single-letter and very short alphabetic fragments, judged in context.
Non-English or mixed-script word pieces not otherwise classifiable.
Emoji and pictographic symbols outside punctuation or mathematical notation.
Standalone or attached algebraic variables and Greek-letter name pieces.
Anything not confidently assigned above, including rare symbols and fragments.
